scope_statement: Apply the analytical framework to a concrete platform case using only publicly available data and documents, deriving empirical implications for strategy and regulation.
must_cover: Brief platform profile and relevant user and provider segments
Define market boundaries relevant for framework application
Identify direct and indirect network effects, positive and negative
Assess multi-homing prevalence and switching costs evidence
Analyze governance changes and related quality indicators
Describe pricing, fees, commissions, and monetization evolution
Evaluate competitive dynamics using market-share indicators
should_cover: Use only publicly available data and documents
Triangulate findings across multiple independent sources
Discuss strategic and regulatory implications of findings
Explicitly state data limitations and evidence strength
must_avoid: Introducing new theory beyond the framework
Use of proprietary or non-public data sources
Primary data collection such as interviews or surveys without permission
Unsupported speculation or policy prescriptions without evidence
main_query: platform empirical case study network effects governance pricing market share public data
facet_queries: platform empirical case study public data network effects
direct indirect network effects evidence platform case study
platform governance changes ranking access rules analysis
platform monetization fees commissions historical changes
market boundary definition two-sided markets case study
platform market share concentration indicators HHI empirical
competition dynamics among platforms empirical evidence
case study methodology secondary data document analysis
scoring_guidance: Score relevance by: empirical alignment with framework (40%), data source quality and public availability (25%), coverage of network effects/governance/pricing/competition (25%), and methodological transparency plus recency (10%). Prioritize sources that directly analyze platform cases using public documents.
